pharm: Carotid chemoreceptor stimulant that increases respiratory drive; at higher doses acts directly on the medullary respiratory centers to increase tidal volume and, to a lesser extent, respiratory rate.
quick: Postanesthesia respiratory depression: 0.5-1 mg/kg IV, may repeat every 5 min; max 2 mg/kg as a single injection (max 4 mg/kg by infusion)
Given parenterally (IV); not related to meals
Former category B; no adequate human data - use only if clearly needed
No data on transfer into milk; use with caution
No specific dose adjustment in labeling; use lowest effective dose
No specific dose adjustment; metabolized hepatically - monitor
Not relevant to acute IV use; alcohol is a CNS depressant the drug may counter
Respiratory rate, ABG/blood gases, BP, heart rhythm, deep tendon reflexes (avoid overdose/seizures)
summary: Doxapram is a parenteral central respiratory stimulant (analeptic) used short-term in hospital settings to stimulate respiration in drug-induced postanesthesia respiratory depression or apnea (not muscle-relaxant induced), to aid arousal and ventilation in mild-to-moderate drug-induced CNS depression, and as a temporary measure in acute hypercapnia complicating chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. It acts primarily through the peripheral carotid chemoreceptors at low doses and on the medullary respiratory centers at higher doses, increasing tidal volume. It has a narrow margin of safety: excessive dosing can cause hypertension, tachycardia, arrhythmias, muscle hyperactivity and convulsions. It is contraindicated in epilepsy/seizure disorders, severe cardiovascular disease, severe hypertension, head injury, stroke, mechanical airway/ventilation problems and pneumothorax. It must never be used as a substitute for mechanical ventilation or as a narcotic antagonist.
indications: Drug-induced postanesthesia respiratory depression or apnea (other than that due to muscle relaxants) - to stimulate respiration
Pharmacologically induced central nervous system depression of mild to moderate severity - to hasten arousal and encourage spontaneous ventilation
Acute hypercapnia superimposed on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) - as a temporary measure in hospitalized patients

dosage.d: 0.5-1 mg/kg as a single injection; may repeat every 5 minutes; maximum single injection 1.5 mg/kg and maximum total 2 mg/kg
dosage.n: Do not exceed 2 mg/kg as single injection

dosage.d: Start 5 mg/min until adequate response, then maintain at 1-3 mg/min; maximum total 4 mg/kg (about 300 mg)
Priming dose 1-2 mg/kg IV, repeated at 1-2 hour intervals until patient awakens (or relapse occurs); IV infusion may follow at up to 1-3 mg/min; maximum 3 grams in 24 hours
1-3 mg/minute by IV infusion; maximum duration of infusion is 2 hours
dosage.n: Monitor blood gases; temporary measure only

admin: Administer by intravenous injection or controlled IV infusion only; ensure airway is patent and oxygenation is adequate before use
Use an infusion pump or microdrip for controlled infusion; titrate against respiratory response
Maintain continuous monitoring of respiration, blood pressure, heart rhythm and deep tendon reflexes during and for 30-60 minutes after administration
Have resuscitation and anticonvulsant therapy (e.g., short-acting barbiturate/benzodiazepine), oxygen and intubation equipment immediately available
After general anesthesia with volatile agents that sensitize the myocardium, delay doxapram until the anesthetic is largely eliminated to avoid arrhythmias
moa: Doxapram produces respiratory stimulation mediated through the peripheral carotid chemoreceptors at low (subconvulsant) doses; with increasing dose it also acts directly on the medullary respiratory centers in the brainstem. The result is an increase in tidal volume with a slight increase in respiratory rate, raising minute ventilation. Its respiratory stimulant action is accompanied at higher doses by general CNS stimulation, which accounts for its narrow margin between respiratory stimulation and convulsant/sympathomimetic toxicity. It is not a narcotic antagonist and does not reverse opioid- or muscle-relaxant-induced depression specifically.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to doxapram or any component

Mechanical disorders of ventilation: airway obstruction, muscle paresis, flail chest, pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, acute bronchial asthma, pulmonary fibrosis or other conditions resulting in restricted chest wall, muscular or alveolar expansion
Severe coronary artery disease, uncompensated heart failure, severe hypertension including that associated with pheochromocytoma
Cerebrovascular accident (stroke) or significant head injury
Should not be used in conjunction with mechanical ventilation
relative: Hypoxia or hypercapnia at risk of worsening if ventilation is inadequate
Patients receiving sympathomimetics or MAO inhibitors (additive pressor effect)
Neonates and infants (benzyl alcohol preservative - gasping syndrome risk)
Patients with cardiac arrhythmias or significant cardiovascular disease
monitor: Respiratory rate and arterial blood gases
Deep tendon reflexes (hyperreflexia warns of impending overdose/convulsions)
Level of consciousness and signs of recurrent narcosis

preg: Former pregnancy category B. Reproduction studies in animals did not demonstrate fetal harm, but there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether doxapram is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when administering to a nursing woman; given its short-term acute use, breastfeeding decisions are usually individualized.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is provided in the labeling. Because doxapram and its active metabolite are renally cleared, use the lowest effective dose and monitor closely in renal impairment.
hepatic: Doxapram is extensively metabolized in the liver (including ring hydroxylation to the active metabolite ketodoxapram). No specific dose adjustment is given, but caution and close monitoring are advised in hepatic impairment.

major: MAO inhibitors and sympathomimetic amines - additive pressor effect; may cause marked hypertension; avoid or use with extreme caution
Skeletal muscle relaxants - doxapram may temporarily mask residual neuromuscular blockade, producing apparent recovery followed by re-paralysis
moderate: Volatile inhalation anesthetics (halothane, enflurane, etc.) - increased risk of cardiac arrhythmias; delay doxapram until anesthetic largely eliminated
Aminophylline/theophylline - additive CNS stimulation causing increased skeletal muscle activity and agitation
minor: Drugs that increase catecholamine release may augment cardiovascular response
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol is a CNS depressant; doxapram is sometimes used in CNS depressant overdose, but routine concurrent intake is not relevant to acute IV therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: Doxapram may produce a mild increase in plasma catecholamines; monitor blood gases (may transiently lower PaCO2 and raise PaO2).

common: Increased blood pressure and heart rate
serious: Cardiac arrhythmias including ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation
rare: Urinary retention or involuntary urination/bladder stimulation
Thrombophlebitis at the injection site / extravasation injury
emergency: Acute respiratory failure if used inappropriately in place of ventilation

monitoring: Continuous respiratory rate and arterial blood gas monitoring during therapy
Blood pressure and continuous ECG/cardiac rhythm monitoring
Deep tendon reflexes - hyperreflexia signals impending overdose
Level of consciousness; observe for recurrent narcosis for at least 30-60 minutes after the patient appears alert
counsel: This is an emergency hospital medicine given by injection to help you breathe; it is administered and monitored by the care team
Tell the team if you have epilepsy, heart disease, high blood pressure, or have had a stroke or head injury
You may feel warm, flushed, restless or have a headache - report these and any chest discomfort or palpitations
You will be watched closely for breathing and heart effects during and after the dose
This medicine does not replace a breathing machine or reverse opioid overdose by itself
pk: Respiratory stimulation within 20-40 seconds of IV injection
Short - about 5-12 minutes after a single IV dose
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C (68-77 F)
pearls: Respiratory stimulant with a NARROW safety margin - excessive dosing causes muscle hyperactivity, agitation, arrhythmias and seizures; hyperreflexia is an early warning sign
Never use as a substitute for mechanical ventilation and not as a narcotic antagonist - ensure airway patency and adequate oxygenation first
Contraindicated in seizure disorders, severe cardiovascular disease/severe hypertension, head injury, stroke, and mechanical ventilation problems
Watch for recurrent (rebound) narcosis after the patient appears to recover; observe 30-60 minutes
Older injection contains benzyl alcohol preservative - avoid in neonates (gasping syndrome)
missed: Not applicable - doxapram is given as an acute, titrated intravenous therapy in a monitored hospital setting rather than on a scheduled outpatient regimen. The clinician titrates repeat doses to respiratory response within the stated maximums.
overdose: Overdose is marked by excessive pressor effect, tachycardia, skeletal muscle hyperactivity, hyperreflexia, agitation and generalized convulsions, with risk of cardiac arrhythmias. There is no specific antidote. Discontinue the drug, secure the airway and provide oxygen/ventilatory support, and treat seizures with a short-acting intravenous anticonvulsant (e.g., benzodiazepine or barbiturate). Manage hypertension and arrhythmias symptomatically. Doxapram is dialyzable.
